whatChanged.title: Automation moved from concept coverage toward deployment stories
whatChanged.detail: Factory, warehouse, and humanoid pilot stories appeared more often than generic robotics hype.

whatChanged.title: The theme gained relevance inside Technology
whatChanged.detail: Robotics-automation became a clearer sibling to AI infrastructure rather than a niche subtopic.

whyItMatters.summary: A durable robotics theme signals real-world adoption and industrial workflow change rather than isolated prototype headlines.
statements: Repeated deployment evidence matters more than eye-catching demo videos.
Robotics often becomes structurally important when it attaches to labor scarcity, cost pressure, and manufacturing throughput.
The right question is whether deployment breadth is widening, not whether one robot launch went viral.

requiredClaims: The quarterly aggregate should show persistent coverage rather than a one-week spike.
Coverage should reference deployments, supply chains, or integrators, not only concept demos.
At least one company or buyer class should recur across the quarter.
provenanceExpectations: Use deployment and procurement stories as higher-grade evidence than product teaser content.
Expect future SEC and hiring signals to strengthen this brief.
notes: Humanoid excitement alone is not enough to call the theme structurally stronger.

subtopicMovement.rationale: Line-side and warehouse deployment is the strongest recurring signal.
Humanoid systems are drawing attention, but still need real deployment proof.
Middleware and orchestration are less visible but may become the better structural signal.

pathways.note: Industrial automation exposure gives TER a plausible public-market link.
Large industrial automation players often confirm whether adoption is broadening.
Repeated manufacturer pilots help separate deployment evidence from robotics hype.

risks.title: Demo-video bias
risks.detail: Visual novelty can overwhelm weak commercialization evidence.

risks.title: AI narrative bleed
risks.detail: Generic AI headlines can leak into robotics unless deployment-specific terms are present.

watchpoints.trigger: A second wave of deployment stories lands outside one flagship vendor
watchpoints.implication: Confidence rises that the theme is broadening rather than concentrating.

watchpoints.trigger: Filings, capex commentary, or supplier disclosures mention robotics demand
watchpoints.implication: The theme gets stronger links to real operating budgets.

prompts: Which robotics subtheme is gaining share because of real deployment rather than narrative spillover?
What evidence would show robotics is becoming budgeted infrastructure instead of optional experimentation?

notes: Use this file to catch regressions where generated briefs over-index on hype and under-index on deployment evidence.
